relations.myth: Sophia produces and hides the ignorant ruler
relations.note: Sophia generates Saklas without her consort and hides her malformed offspring.

relations.myth: Saklas retains Sophia's luminous power
relations.note: Saklas steals or retains part of Sophia's light-power, enabling his creation.

relations.myth: Saklas seizes the descended Epinoia's power
relations.note: Saklas overpowers Light Epinoia and takes power from her after her descent.

relations.myth: Pronoia tricks Saklas into empowering Adam
relations.note: Pronoia secretly causes Saklas to transfer Sophia's stolen power into Adam.

relations.myth: The revealer enters Saklas's creation
relations.note: Christ exposes Saklas's ignorance and descends into his cosmos to awaken humanity.

relations.myth: Zoe binds Saklas and casts him down
relations.note: Zoe rebukes Saklas; her fiery angel binds him and casts him into Tartarus.

relations.myth: Pistis Sophia supports Sabaoth's elevation
relations.note: Pistis Sophia opposes Saklas indirectly by supporting his rebellious son's promotion.
Sabaoth is a son and subordinate authority generated by Saklas.

relations.myth: Sabaoth rebels against his father
relations.note: Sabaoth recognizes Saklas's error, condemns him, and joins the higher order.

relations.myth: Eleleth produces the lower rulers
relations.note: Eleleth produces or authorizes Saklas and Nebro within the lower cosmic order.

relations.myth: Nebro creates Saklas as an assistant
relations.note: Nebro creates six angels and Saklas to serve as lower-cosmic assistants.

relations.myth: Nebro and Saklas organize the lower heavens
relations.note: Nebro and Saklas jointly organize the rulers and administration of the lower heavens.

relations.myth: Three names of the chief ruler
relations.note: Saklas and Yaldabaoth are names of one ruler in several Sethian texts.

relations.myth: Three names of the chief ruler
relations.note: Saklas and Samael are co-referential names in the three-name textual tradition.

relations.myth: Jesus exposes sacrifice offered to Saklas
relations.note: Jesus identifies the disciples' corrupted worship and sacrifices as service to Saklas.

relations.myth: Judas sacrifices the body clothing Jesus
relations.note: Judas's disputed sacrifice of Jesus's mortal body is associated with sacrifice to Saklas.

relations.myth: Saklas copies the Messenger's displayed beauty
relations.note: Saklas and his partner imitate the Third Messenger's male-female form when making humanity.
Nebroel and her regional equivalents are Saklas's female procreative partner.

relations.myth: Demonic partners fashion Adam and Eve
relations.note: Together they consume light-bearing offspring, copulate, and fashion the first human couple.
relations.source: Coptic, Iranian, and Syriac Manichaean texts

relations.myth: Āz devises humanity as a light-prison
relations.note: Saklas and his partner function as embodiments, garments, or instruments of Āz.
Saklas belongs to the demonic order remotely headed by the King of Darkness.

relations.myth: Saklas's authorities fashion Adam
relations.note: Saklas directs Adam's bodily formation, while higher powers provide his spiritual animation.

relations.myth: Saklas commands Adam's creation
relations.note: Saklas orders his angels to make Adam after the likeness and image.

relations.myth: Demonic partners concentrate light in Adam
relations.note: Saklas and his partner fashion Adam as an image and prison of divine light.

relations.myth: Saklas commands Eve's creation
relations.note: Saklas commands the creation of Eve alongside Adam.

relations.myth: Demonic partners concentrate light in Eve
relations.note: Saklas and his partner fashion Eve as an image and prison of divine light.

relations.myth: Saklas seduces Eve
relations.note: Some comparatively late Manichaean reports portray Saklas or his counterpart seducing Eve.

relations.myth: Saklas attempts to destroy Seth
relations.note: Saklas or the related al-Ṣendīd attacks Seth, whom Adam saves.

relations.myth: Saklas persecutes Seth's incorruptible race
relations.note: Saklas seeks to destroy or enslave heavenly Seth and his incorruptible seed.
relations.source: Holy Book of the Great Invisible Spirit

relations.note: Modern harmonizations identify Saklas directly with Yahweh beyond the texts' qualified creator polemic.
Modern occult and internet interpretations identify Saklas with Satan without universal ancient support.
Modern syncretism identifies Saklas with Lucifer; no ancient interaction is documented.
Popular Jungian synthesis sometimes equates Abraxas with Saklas, though they are not ancient synonyms.
